rationale: IT admins at SMBs and non-profits self-hosting Bitwarden are identifiable buyers, but this segment is specifically cost-sensitive (they chose self-hosted precisely to avoid the paid tier), making willingness_to_pay weak at 4. More critically, the solution — adding granular access controls to a self-hosted Bitwarden instance — requires building a companion admin layer that interfaces with Bitwarden's internal API or modifying deployment configs, which is meaningful engineering work (buildability_with_ai=4) and requires per-deployment customization and support (operational_autonomy=4). solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable for the autonomous factory model at this stage. Adding policy controls to self-hosted Bitwarden requires either a custom reverse proxy layer with policy enforcement logic, or integration with Bitwarden's organization management API — both require real software engineering to build and per-deployment support to maintain. The buyer segment (non-profits, cost-sensitive SMBs) is also the segment least likely to pay for an add-on tool. This could theoretically be explored as a managed Bitwarden deployment service, but that would require ongoing infrastructure management, which is outside scope.
